description:
<{["RT", "بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ"]}>

In the Name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

<{["RT", "طسم - تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ - لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ - إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ - وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ - فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَاءُ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ - أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ - إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ - وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ", "1. Ta Sin Mim. 2. These are Ayat of the Book Mubin. 3. It may be that you are going Bakhi' yourself, that they do not become believers. 4. If We will, We could send down to them from the heaven a sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility. 5. And never comes there unto them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious, but they turn away therefrom. 6. So, they have indeed denied, then the news of what they mocked at will come to them. 7. Do they not observe the earth – how much of every good kind We cause to grow therein? 8. Verily, in this is an Ayah, yet most of them are not believers. 9. And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful."]}>

## The Qur'an and the Disbelievers Turning Away; They Could Be Compelled to Believe If Allah so Willed

At the beginning of the explanation of Surat Al-Baqarah we discussed the letters which appear at the beginning of some Surahs. Allah's saying:

<{["RT", "تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ", "These are the Ayat of the Book Mubin."]}>

means, these are the verses of the Clear Qur'an, i.e. the clear and unambiguous Book which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, misguidance and guidance.

<{["RT", "لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ", "It may be that you are going Bakhi' yourself,"]}>

means, destroy yourself – because of your keenness that they should be guided and your grief for them.

<{["RT", "أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ", "that they do not become believers."]}>

Here Allah is consoling His Messenger ﷺ for the lack of faith of those among the disbelievers who do not believe in him. This is like the Ayat:

<{["RT", "فَلَا تَذْهَبْ نَفْسُكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَسَرَاتٍ", "So destroy not yourself in sorrow for them (<{[\"Q\", \"35:8\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ عَلَىٰ آثَارِهِمْ إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَٰذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا", "Perhaps, you would Bakhi' yourself, over their footsteps, because they believe not in this narration (<{[\"Q\", \"18:6\"]}>)"]}>

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah, Ad-Dahhak, Al-Hasan and others said that:

<{["RT", "لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ", "It may be that you are going Bakhi' yourself,"]}>

means, 'kill yourself.' Then Allah says:

<{["RT", "إِن نَّشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِم مِّنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ", "If We will, We could send down to them from the heaven a sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility."]}>

Meaning: 'if We so willed, We could send down a sign that would force them to believe, but We will not do that because We do not want anyone to believe except by choice.' Allah says:

<{["RT", "وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَآمَنَ مَن فِي الْأَرْضِ كُلُّهُمْ جَمِيعًا ۚ أَفَأَنتَ تُكْرِهُ النَّاسَ حَتَّىٰ يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ", "And had your Lord willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together. So, will you then compel mankind, until they become believers. (<{[\"Q\", \"10:99\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَلَوْ شَاءَ رَبُّكَ لَجَعَلَ النَّاسَ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً", "And if your Lord had so willed, He could surely, have made mankind one Ummah... (<{[\"Q\", \"11:118\"]}>)"]}>

But Allah's will has acted, His decree has come to pass, and His proof has been conveyed to mankind by mission of Messengers and the revelation of Books to them. Then Allah says:

<{["RT", "وَمَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن ذِكْرٍ مِّنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ", "And never comes there unto them a Reminder as a recent revelation from the Most Gracious, but they turn away therefrom."]}>

Meaning: every time a Scripture comes from heaven to them, most of the people turn away from it. As Allah says:

<{["RT", "وَمَا أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ وَلَوْ حَرَصْتَ بِمُؤْمِنِينَ", "And most of mankind will not believe even if you desire it eagerly. (<{[\"Q\", \"12:103\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "يَا حَسْرَةً عَلَى الْعِبَادِ ۚ مَا يَأْتِيهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ", "Alas for mankind! There never came a Messenger to them but they used to mock at him. (<{[\"Q\", \"36:30\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنَا رُسُلَنَا تَتْرَىٰ ۖ كُلَّ مَا جَاءَ أُمَّةً رَّسُولُهَا كَذَّبُوهُ", "Then We sent Our Messengers in succession. Every time there came to a nation their Messenger, they denied him... (<{[\"Q\", \"23:44\"]}>)"]}>

Allah says here:

<{["RT", "فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنبَاءُ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ", "So, they have indeed denied, then the news of what they mocked at will come to them."]}>

Meaning: they denied the truth that came to them, so they will come to know the news of the consequences of this denial after a while.

<{["RT", "وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ", "And those who do wrong will come to know by what overturning they will be overturned (<{[\"Q\", \"26:227\"]}>)"]}>

Then Allah tells those who dared to oppose His Messenger ﷺ and disbelieve in His Book, that He is the Subduer, the Almighty, the All-Powerful, Who created the earth and caused every good kind of crop, fruit and animal to grow therein. Sufyan Ath-Thawri narrated from a man from Ash-Sha'bi that people are a product of the earth. So whoever enters Paradise is good and noble, and whoever enters Hell is base and vile.

<{["RT", "إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً", "Verily, in this is an Ayah,"]}>

meaning an evidence of the power of the Creator of all things. He spread out the earth and raised the canopy of the heavens, yet despite that the majority of people do not believe, rather they deny Him, His Messengers, and His Books, and they go against His commands doing the things He had prohibited. His saying:

4.1: i.e., they would be compelled to believe.

16.1: The singular form in Arabic indicates that both were sent with a single message.

19.1: i.e., striking the Copt, who died as a result.

38.1: i.e., the morning of the day of festival. See <{["Q", "20:58"]}>-<{["Q", "20:59", "59"]}>.

53.1: Recruiters of an army to prevent the emigration of the Children of Israel.

58.1: Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) caused them to abandon their wealth and property in pursuit of the Israelites.

77.1: The people worshipped idols in addition to Allāh.

102.1: The conclusion of this verse is estimated as "...we would do this or that."

128.1: i.e., a symbol or indication of their wealth and power. They used to build lofty structures along the road to be seen by all who passed by.

155.1: Miraculously sent to them as a sign by Allāh.

165.1: i.e., Are there, out of all Allāh's creatures, any besides you who commit this unnatural act?

171.1: Lut's wife, who had collaborated with the evildoers.

198.1: i.e., the non-Arabs or those who are not fluent in the Arabic language.

210.1: As was asserted by the disbelievers. Rather, it was brought by Gabriel, the Trustworthy Spirit.

218.1: From your bed at night for prayer while you are alone.

219.1: i.e., among those who pray with you in congregation.

223.1: This was before they were prevented, as described in <{["Q", "72:8"]}>-<{["Q", "72:9", "9"]}>.

225.1: Speaking lies indiscriminately and praising and disparaging others according to whim.

227.1: By replying through poetry to the attacks of hostile poets.

translations.2: These are the verses of the clear Book.
translations.3: Perhaps, [O Muḥammad], you would kill yourself with grief that they will not be believers.
translations.4: If We willed, We could send down to them from the sky a sign for which their necks would remain humbled.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.5: And no mention [i.e., revelation] comes to them anew from the Most Merciful except that they turn away from it.
translations.6: For they have already denied, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to ridicule.
translations.7: Did they not look at the earth - how much We have produced therein from every noble kind?
translations.8: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.9: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.10: And [mention] when your Lord called Musa, [saying], "Go to the wrongdoing people -
translations.11: The people of Pharaoh. Will they not fear Allāh?"
translations.12: He said, "My Lord, indeed I fear that they will deny me
translations.13: And that my breast will tighten and my tongue will not be fluent, so send for Harun.
translations.14: And they have upon me a [claim due to] sin, so I fear that they will kill me."
translations.15: [Allāh] said, "No. Go both of you with Our signs; indeed, We are with you, listening.
translations.16: Go to Pharaoh and say, 'We are the messengers<{["F", 1]}> of the Lord of the worlds,
translations.17: [Commanded to say], "Send with us the Children of Israel."'"
translations.18: [Pharaoh] said, "Did we not raise you among us as a child, and you remained among us for years of your life?
translations.19: And [then] you did your deed which you did,<{["F", 1]}> and you were of the ungrateful."
translations.20: [Musa] said, "I did it, then, while I was of those astray [i.e., ignorant].
translations.21: So I fled from you when I feared you. Then my Lord granted me judgement [i.e., wisdom and prophethood] and appointed me [as one] of the messengers.
translations.22: And is this a favor of which you remind me - that you have enslaved the Children of Israel?"
translations.23: Said Pharaoh, "And what is the Lord of the worlds?"
translations.24: [Musa] said, "The Lord of the heavens and earth and that between them, if you should be convinced."
translations.25: [Pharaoh] said to those around him, "Do you not hear?"
translations.26: [Musa] said, "Your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers."
translations.27: [Pharaoh] said,<{["F", 1]}> "Indeed, your 'messenger' who has been sent to you is mad."
translations.28: [Musa] said, "Lord of the east and the west and that between them, if you were to reason."
translations.29: [Pharaoh] said, "If you take a god other than me, I will surely place you among those imprisoned."
translations.30: [Musa] said, "Even if I brought you something [i.e., proof] manifest?"
translations.31: [Pharaoh] said, "Then bring it, if you should be of the truthful."
translations.32: So [Musa] threw his staff, and suddenly it was a serpent manifest.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.33: And he drew out his hand; thereupon it was white for the observers.
translations.34: [Pharaoh] said to the eminent ones around him, "Indeed, this is a learned magician.
translations.35: He wants to drive you out of your land by his magic, so what do you advise?"
translations.36: They said, "Postpone [the matter of] him and his brother and send among the cities gatherers
translations.37: Who will bring you every learned, skilled magician."
translations.38: So the magicians were assembled for the appointment of a well-known day.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.39: And it was said to the people, "Will you congregate
translations.40: That we might follow the magicians if they are the predominant?"
translations.41: And when the magicians arrived, they said to Pharaoh, "Is there indeed for us a reward if we are the predominant?"
translations.42: He said, "Yes, and indeed, you will then be of those near [to me]."
translations.43: Musa said to them, "Throw whatever you will throw."
translations.44: So they threw their ropes and their staffs and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, indeed it is we who are predominant."
translations.45: Then Musa threw his staff, and at once it devoured what they falsified.
translations.46: So the magicians fell down in prostration [to Allāh].
translations.47: They said, "We have believed in the Lord of the worlds,
translations.48: The Lord of Musa and Harun."
translations.49: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Musa] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic, but you are going to know. I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you all."
translations.50: They said, "No harm. Indeed, to our Lord we will return.
translations.51: Indeed, we aspire that our Lord will forgive us our sins because we were the first of the believers."
translations.52: And We inspired to Musa, "Travel by night with My servants; indeed, you will be pursued."
translations.53: Then Pharaoh sent among the cities gatherers<{["F", 1]}>
translations.54: [And said], "Indeed, those are but a small band,
translations.55: And indeed, they are enraging us,
translations.56: And indeed, we are a cautious society..."
translations.57: So We removed them from gardens and springs
translations.59: Thus. And We caused to inherit it the Children of Israel.
translations.60: So they pursued them at sunrise.
translations.61: And when the two companies saw one another, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are to be overtaken!"
translations.62: [Musa] said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."
translations.63: Then We inspired to Musa, "Strike with your staff the sea," and it parted, and each portion was like a great towering mountain.
translations.64: And We advanced thereto the others [i.e., the pursuers].
translations.65: And We saved Musa and those with him, all together.
translations.67: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.68: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.69: And recite to them the news of Ibrahim,
translations.70: When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"
translations.71: They said, "We worship idols and remain to them devoted."
translations.72: He said, "Do they hear you when you supplicate?
translations.73: Or do they benefit you, or do they harm?"
translations.74: They said, "But we found our fathers doing thus."
translations.75: He said, "Then do you see what you have been worshipping,
translations.77: Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds,<{["F", 1]}>
translations.78: Who created me, and He [it is who] guides me.
translations.79: And it is He who feeds me and gives me drink.
translations.80: And when I am ill, it is He who cures me
translations.81: And who will cause me to die and then bring me to life
translations.82: And who I aspire that He will forgive me my sin on the Day of Recompense."
translations.83: [And he said], "My Lord, grant me authority and join me with the righteous.
translations.84: And grant me a mention [i.e., reputation] of honor among later generations.
translations.85: And place me among the inheritors of the Garden of Pleasure.
translations.86: And forgive my father. Indeed, he has been of those astray.
translations.87: And do not disgrace me on the Day they are [all] resurrected -
translations.88: The Day when there will not benefit [anyone] wealth or children
translations.89: But only one who comes to Allāh with a sound heart."
translations.90: And Paradise will be brought near [that Day] to the righteous.
translations.91: And Hellfire will be brought forth for the deviators,
translations.92: And it will be said to them, "Where are those you used to worship
translations.93: Other than Allāh? Can they help you or help themselves?"
translations.94: So they will be overturned into it [i.e., Hellfire], they and the deviators
translations.95: And the soldiers of Iblees, all together.
translations.96: They will say while they dispute therein,
translations.97: "By Allāh, we were indeed in manifest error
translations.98: When we equated you with the Lord of the worlds.
translations.99: And no one misguided us except the criminals.
translations.100: So now we have no intercessors
translations.102: Then if we only had a return [to the world] and could be of the believers..."<{["F", 1]}>
translations.103: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.104: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.105: The people of Nuh denied the messengers<{["F", 1]}>
translations.106: When their brother Nuh said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?
translations.107: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
translations.108: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.109: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
translations.110: So fear Allāh and obey me."
translations.111: They said, "Should we believe you while you are followed by the lowest [class of people]?"
translations.112: He said, "And what is my knowledge of what they used to do?
translations.113: Their account is only upon my Lord, if you [could] perceive.
translations.114: And I am not one to drive away the believers.
translations.115: I am only a clear warner."
translations.116: They said, "If you do not desist, O Nuh, you will surely be of those who are stoned."
translations.117: He said, "My Lord, indeed my people have denied me.
translations.118: Then judge between me and them with decisive judgement and save me and those with me of the believers."
translations.119: So We saved him and those with him in the laden ship.
translations.120: Then We drowned thereafter the remaining ones.
translations.121: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.122: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.124: When their brother Hūd said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?
translations.125: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
translations.126: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.127: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
translations.128: Do you construct on every elevation a sign,<{["F", 1]}> amusing yourselves,
translations.129: And take for yourselves constructions [i.e., palaces and fortresses] that you might abide eternally?
translations.130: And when you strike, you strike as tyrants.
translations.131: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.132: And fear He who provided you with that which you know,
translations.133: Provided you with grazing livestock and children
translations.135: Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a terrible day."
translations.136: They said, "It is all the same to us whether you advise or are not of the advisors.
translations.137: This is not but the custom of the former peoples,
translations.138: And we are not to be punished."
translations.139: And they denied him, so We destroyed them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.140: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.142: When their brother Ṣāliḥ said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?
translations.143: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
translations.144: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.145: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
translations.146: Will you be left in what is here, secure [from death],
translations.148: And fields of crops and palm trees with softened fruit?
translations.149: And you carve out of the mountains, homes, with skill.
translations.150: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.151: And do not obey the order of the transgressors,
translations.152: Who cause corruption in the land and do not amend."
translations.153: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.
translations.154: You are but a man like ourselves, so bring a sign, if you should be of the truthful."
translations.155: He said, "This is a she-camel.<{["F", 1]}> For her is a [time of] drink, and for you is a [time of] drink, [each] on a known day.
translations.156: And do not touch her with harm, lest you be seized by the punishment of a terrible day."
translations.157: But they hamstrung her and so became regretful.
translations.158: And the punishment seized them. Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.159: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.160: The people of Lut denied the messengers
translations.161: When their brother Lut said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?
translations.162: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
translations.163: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.164: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
translations.165: Do you approach males among the worlds<{["F", 1]}>
translations.166: And leave what your Lord has created for you as mates? But you are a people transgressing."
translations.167: They said, "If you do not desist, O Lut, you will surely be of those evicted."
translations.168: He said, "Indeed, I am, toward your deed, of those who detest [it].
translations.169: My Lord, save me and my family from [the consequence of] what they do."
translations.170: So We saved him and his family, all,
translations.171: Except an old woman<{["F", 1]}> among those who remained behind.
translations.173: And We rained upon them a rain [of stones], and evil was the rain of those who were warned.
translations.174: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.175: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.176: The companions of the thicket [i.e., the people of Madyan] denied the messengers
translations.177: When Shuʿayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allāh?
translations.178: Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
translations.179: So fear Allāh and obey me.
translations.180: And I do not ask you for it any payment. My payment is only from the Lord of the worlds.
translations.181: Give full measure and do not be of those who cause loss.
translations.182: And weigh with an even [i.e., honest] balance.
translations.183: And do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.
translations.184: And fear He who created you and the former creation."<{["F", 1]}>
translations.185: They said, "You are only of those affected by magic.
translations.186: You are but a man like ourselves, and indeed, we think you are among the liars.
translations.187: So cause to fall upon us fragments of the sky, if you should be of the truthful."
translations.188: He said, "My Lord is most knowing of what you do."
translations.189: And they denied him, so the punishment of the day of the black cloud seized them. Indeed, it was the punishment of a terrible day.
translations.190: Indeed in that is a sign, but most of them were not to be believers.
translations.191: And indeed, your Lord - He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
translations.192: And indeed, it [i.e., the Qur’ān] is the revelation of the Lord of the worlds.
translations.193: The Trustworthy Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] has brought it down
translations.194: Upon your heart, [O Muḥammad] - that you may be of the warners
translations.196: And indeed, it is [mentioned] in the scriptures of former peoples.
translations.197: And has it not been a sign to them that it is recognized by the scholars of the Children of Israel?
translations.198: And even if We had revealed it to one among the foreigners<{["F", 1]}>
translations.199: And he had recited it to them [perfectly],<{["F", 1]}> they would [still] not have been believers in it.
translations.200: Thus have We inserted it [i.e., disbelief] into the hearts of the criminals.
translations.201: They will not believe in it until they see the painful punishment.
translations.202: And it will come to them suddenly while they perceive [it] not.
translations.203: And they will say, "May we be reprieved?"
translations.204: So for Our punishment are they impatient?
translations.205: Then have you considered if We gave them enjoyment for years
translations.206: And then there came to them that which they were promised?
translations.207: They would not be availed by the enjoyment with which they were provided.
translations.208: And We did not destroy any city except that it had warners
translations.209: As a reminder; and never have We been unjust.
translations.210: And the devils have not brought it [i.e., the revelation] down.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.211: It is not allowable for them, nor would they be able.
translations.212: Indeed they, from [its] hearing, are removed.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.213: So do not invoke<{["F", 1]}> with Allāh another deity and [thus] be among the punished.
translations.214: And warn, [O Muḥammad], your closest kindred.
translations.215: And lower your wing [i.e., show kindness] to those who follow you of the believers.
translations.216: And if they disobey you, then say, "Indeed, I am disassociated from what you are doing."
translations.217: And rely upon the Exalted in Might, the Merciful,
translations.218: Who sees you when you arise<{["F", 1]}>
translations.219: And your movement among those who prostrate.<{["F", 1]}>
translations.220: Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
translations.221: Shall I inform you upon whom the devils descend?
translations.222: They descend upon every sinful liar.
translations.223: They pass on what is heard,<{["F", 1]}> and most of them are liars.
translations.224: And the poets - [only] the deviators follow them.
translations.225: Do you not see that in every valley they roam<{["F", 1]}>

translations.227: Except those [poets] who believe and do righteous deeds and remember Allāh often and defend [the Muslims]<{["F", 1]}> after they were wronged. And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.

exegesis.1:
<{["RT", "وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ", "And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty,"]}>

means, the One Who has power over all things, to subdue and control them:

<{["RT", "الرَّحِيمُ", "the Most Merciful."]}>

means, towards His creation, for He does not hasten to punish the one who sins, but He gives him time to repent, and if he does not, then He seizes him with a mighty punishment. Abu Al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi' bin Anas and Ibn Ishaq said: "He is Almighty in His punishment of those who went against His commands and worshipped others besides Him." Sa'id bin Jubayr said: "He is Most Merciful towards those who repent to Him and turn to Him."
exegesis.10:
And _(remember)_ when your Lord called Musa _(saying)_: "Go to the people who are wrongdoers (<{["Q", "26:10"]}>). "The people of Fira'wn. Will they not have Taqwa? (<{["Q", "26:11"]}>). He said: "My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will deny me, (<{["Q", "26:12"]}>). "And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Harun (<{["Q", "26:13"]}>). "And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me (<{["Q", "26:14"]}>). _(Allah)_ said: "Nay! Go you both with Our signs. Verily, We shall be with you, listening (<{["Q", "26:15"]}>). "And go both of you to Fira'wn, and say: 'We are the Messengers of the Lord of Al-'Alamin, (<{["Q", "26:16"]}>). 'So allow the Children of Israel to go with us.' (<{["Q", "26:17"]}>). _(Fir'awn)_ said _(to Musa)_: "Did we not bring you up among us as a child? And you did dwell many years of your life with us (<{["Q", "26:18"]}>). "And you did your deed, which you did. While you were one of the ingrates (<{["Q", "26:19"]}>). Musa said: "I did it then, when I was in error (<{["Q", "26:20"]}>). "So, I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord has granted me Hukm, and made me one of the Messengers (<{["Q", "26:21"]}>). "And this is the past favor with which you reproach me, – that you have enslaved the Children of Israel (<{["Q", "26:22"]}>).

## Between Musa and Fir'awn

Allah tells us what He commanded His servant, son of 'Imran and Messenger Musa, peace be upon him, who spoke with Him, to do, when He called him from the right side of the mountain, and conversed with him, and chose him, sent him, and commanded him to go to Fir'awn and his people. Allah says:

<{["RT", "أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ - قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ - قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ - وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلَا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ - وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ", "(And when your Lord called Musa:) \"Go to the people who are wrongdoers. The people of Fir'awn. Will they not have Taqwa?\" He said: \"My Lord! Verily, I fear that they will deny me, And my breast straitens, and my tongue expresses not well. So send for Harun. And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me.\""]}>

So, Musa asked Allah to remove these difficulties for him, as he said in Surah Ta Ha:

<{["RT", "قَالَ رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي - وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي", "Musa said: \"O my Lord! Open for me my chest. And ease my task for me.\" (<{[\"Q\", \"20:25\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"20:26\", \"26\"]}>)"]}>

until:

<{["RT", "قَدْ أُوتِيتَ سُؤْلَكَ يَا مُوسَىٰ", "You are granted your request, O Musa! (<{[\"Q\", \"20:36\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ", "And they have a charge of crime against me, and I fear they will kill me."]}>

because he had killed that Egyptian, which was the reason that he left the land of Egypt.

<{["RT", "قَالَ كَلَّا", "(Allah) said: \"Nay!...\""]}>

Allah told him: do not be afraid of anything like that. This is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ وَنَجْعَلُ لَكُمَا سُلْطَانًا", "Allah said: \"We will strengthen your arm through your brother, and give you both power"]}>

Meaning: proof;

<{["RT", "فَلَا يَصِلُونَ إِلَيْكُمَا ۚ بِآيَاتِنَا أَنتُمَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَكُمَا الْغَالِبُونَ", "so they shall not be able to harm you, with Our signs, you two as well as those who follow you will be the victors (<{[\"Q\", \"28:35\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "فَاذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَا ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُم مُّسْتَمِعُونَ", "Go you both with Our signs. Verily, We shall be with you, listening."]}>

This is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ", "I am with you both, hearing and seeing (<{[\"Q\", \"20:46\"]}>)"]}>

Meaning, 'I will be with you by My protection, care, support and help.'

<{["RT", "فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ", "And go both of you to Fir'awn, and say: 'We are the Messengers of the Lord of the all that exists.'"]}>

This is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "إِنَّا رَسُولَا رَبِّكَ", "Verily, we are both Messengers of your Lord (<{[\"Q\", \"20:47\"]}>)"]}>

Which means, 'both of us have been sent to you,'

<{["RT", "أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ", "So allow the Children of Israel to go with us."]}>

Meaning, 'let them go, free them from your captivity, subjugation and torture, for they are the believing servants of Allah, devoted to Him, and with you they are in a position of humiliating torture.' When Musa said that to him, Fir'awn turned away and ignored him completely, regarding him with scorn and thinking little of him. Saying:

<{["RT", "أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدً", "Did we not bring you up among us as a child?"]}>

Meaning: we brought you up among us, in our home and on our bed, we nourished you and did favors for you for many years, and after all that you responded to our kindness in this manner: you killed one of our men and denied our favors to you.' So he said to him:

<{["RT", "وَأَنتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ", "While you were one of the ingrates."]}>

Meaning: one of those who deny favors. This was the view of Ibn 'Abbas and 'Abdur-Rahman bin Zayd bin Aslam, and was the view favored by Ibn Jarir.

<{["RT", "قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَا إِذًا", "(Musa) said: \"I did it then...\""]}>

Meaning: at that time:

<{["RT", "وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ", "when I was in error."]}>

Meaning: 'before revelation was sent to me and before Allah made me a Prophet and sent me with this Message.'

<{["RT", "فَفَرَرْتُ مِنكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ", "So, I fled from you when I feared you. But my Lord has granted me Hukm, and made me one of the Messengers."]}>

means, 'the first situation came to an end and another took its place. Now Allah has sent me to you, and if you obey Him, you will be safe, but if you oppose Him, you will be destroyed.' Then Musa said:

<{["RT", "وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدتَّ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ", "And this is the past favor with which you reproach me, – that you have enslaved the Children of Israel."]}>

Meaning: 'whatever favors you did in bringing me up are offset by the evil you did by enslaving the Children of Israel and using them to do your hard labor. Is there any comparison between your favors to one man among them and the evil you have done to all of them? What you have mentioned about me is nothing compared to what you have done to them.'
exegesis.23:
Fir'awn said: "And what is the Lord of Al-'Alamin (<{["Q", "26:23"]}>). _(Musa)_ said: "The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them, if you seek to be convinced with certainty (<{["Q", "26:24"]}>). _(Fir'awn)_ said to those around: "Do you not hear _(what he says)_? (<{["Q", "26:25"]}>). _(Musa)_ said: "Your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers! (<{["Q", "26:26"]}>). _(Fir'awn)_ said: "Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman! (<{["Q", "26:27"]}>). _(Musa)_ said: "Lord of the east and the west, and all that is between them, if you did but understand! (<{["Q", "26:28"]}>).

## Allah tells us about the disbelief, rebellion, oppression and denial of Fir'awn, as He says:

<{["RT", "وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ", "(Fir'awn said:) \"And what is the Lord of the 'Alamin\""]}>

This is because he used to say to his people:

<{["RT", "مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِي", "I know not that you have a god other than me. (<{[\"Q\", \"28:38\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "فَاسْتَخَفَّ قَوْمَهُ فَأَطَاعُوهُ", "Thus he fooled his people, and they obeyed him. (<{[\"Q\", \"43:54\"]}>)"]}>

They used to deny the Creator, may He be glorified, and they believed that they had no other lord than Fir'awn. When Musa said to them: I am the Messenger of the Lord of the worlds," Fir'awn said to him, "Who is this who you are claiming is the Lord of Al-'Alamin other than me?" This is how it was interpreted by the scholars of the Salaf and the Imams of later generations. As-Suddi said, "This Ayah is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "قَالَ فَمَن رَّبُّكُمَا يَا مُوسَىٰ - قَالَ رَبُّنَا الَّذِي أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ خَلْقَهُ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ", "(Fir'awn) said: \"Who then, O Musa, is the Lord of you two?\" He said: \"Our Lord is He Who gave to each thing its form and nature, then guided it aright.\" (<{[\"Q\", \"20:49\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"20:50\", \"50\"]}>)"]}>

Those among the philosophers and others who claimed that this was a question about the nature or substance _[of Allah]_ are mistaken. Fir'awn did not believe in the Creator in the first place, so he was in no position to ask about the nature of the Creator; he denied that the Creator existed at all, as is apparent from the meaning, even though proof and evidence had been established against him. When Fir'awn asked him about the Lord of Al-'Alamin, Musa said:

<{["RT", "قَالَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا", "(Musa) said: \"The Lord of the heavens and the earth, and all that is between them...\""]}>

Meaning: the Creator, Sovereign and Controller of all that, their God Who has no partner or associate. He is the One Who has created all things. He knows the higher realms and the heavenly bodies that are in them, both those that are stationary and those that move and shine brightly. He knows the lower realms and what is in them; the oceans, continents, mountains, trees, animals, plants and fruits. He knows what is in between the two realms; the winds, birds, and whatever is in the air. All of them are servants to Him, submitting and humbling themselves before Him.

<{["RT", "إِن كُنتُم مُّوقِنِينَ", "if you seek to be convinced with certainty."]}>

means, if you have believing hearts and clear insight. At this, Fir'awn turned to the chiefs and leaders of his state around him, and said to them – mockingly expressing his disbelief in Musa:

<{["RT", "أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ", "\"Do you not hear?\""]}>

Meaning: 'are you not amazed by what this man is claiming – that you have another god other than me' Musa said to them:

<{["RT", "رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ", "Your Lord and the Lord of your ancient fathers!"]}>

Meaning: the One Who created you and your forefathers, those who came before Fir'awn and his time.

<{["RT", "قَالَ", "He said"]}>

that is, Fir'awn said:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ", "Verily, your Messenger who has been sent to you is a madman!"]}>

Meaning: there is no sense in his claim that there is any god other than me!'

<{["RT", "قَالَ", "(Musa) said"]}>

– to those in whose hearts Fir'awn had planted doubts:

<{["RT", "رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ إِن كُنتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ", "Lord of the east and the west, and all that is between them, if you did but understand!"]}>

He is the One Who made the east the place where the heavenly bodies rise, and made the west the place where they set; this is the system to which He has subjugated all the heavenly bodies, stationary and moving. If what Fir'awn claims is true, that he is your lord and your god, then let him turn things around so that the heavenly bodies set in the east and rise in the west.' This is similar to the Ayah:

<{["RT", "الَّذِي حَاجَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ فِي رَبِّهِ أَنْ آتَاهُ اللَّهُ الْمُلْكَ إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ رَبِّيَ الَّذِي يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا أُحْيِي وَأُمِيتُ ۖ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْتِي بِالشَّمْسِ مِنَ الْمَشْرِقِ فَأْتِ بِهَا مِنَ الْمَغْرِبِ", "who disputed with Ibrahim about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom? When Ibrahim said: \"My Lord is He Who gives life and causes death.\" He said, \"I give life and cause death.\" Ibrahim said, \"Verily, Allah brings the sun from the east. So cause it to rise from the west.\" (<{[\"Q\", \"2:258\"]}>)"]}>

So when Fir'awn was defeated in debate, he resorted to the use of his force and power, believing that this would be effective in dealing with Musa, peace be upon him, so he said, as Allah tells us:
exegesis.29:
He said: If you choose a god other than me, I will certainly put you among the prisoners (<{["Q", "26:29"]}>). He said: "Even if I bring you something manifest? (<{["Q", "26:30"]}>). He said: "Bring it forth then, if you are of the truthful! (<{["Q", "26:31"]}>). So he threw his stick, and behold, it was a serpent, manifest (<{["Q", "26:32"]}>). And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to all beholders (<{["Q", "26:33"]}>). He said to the chiefs around him: "Verily, this is indeed a well-versed sorcerer (<{["Q", "26:34"]}>). "He wants to drive you out of your land by his sorcery: what is it then that you command? (<{["Q", "26:35"]}>). They said: "Put him off and his brother _(for a while)_, and send callers to the cities; (<{["Q", "26:36"]}>). "To bring up to you every well-versed sorcerer (<{["Q", "26:37"]}>).

## After the Rational Proof, Fir'awn Resorts to Force

When proof had been established against Fir'awn, clearly and rationally, he resorted to using force against Musa, thinking that after this there would no further room for discussion. So he said:

<{["RT", "لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ", "If you choose a god other than me, I will certainly put you among the prisoners."]}>

To this, Musa responded:

<{["RT", "أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُّبِينٍ", "Even if I bring you something manifest"]}>

Meaning: clear and definitive proof.

<{["RT", "قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِ إِن كُنتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ - فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُّبِينٌ", "Fir'awn said: \"Bring it forth then, if you are of the truthful!\" So he threw his stick, and behold, it was a serpent, manifest."]}>

meanig, it was very clear and obvious, with a huge body and a big mouth, terrifying in appearance.

<{["RT", "وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ", "And he drew out his hand,"]}>

Meaning: from his sleeve:

<{["RT", "فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ", "and behold, it was white to all beholders!"]}>

It was shining like a piece of the moon. Since Fir'awn was already doomed, he hastened to stubborn denial, and said to the chiefs around him:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ", "Verily, this is indeed a well-versed sorcerer."]}>

One who knows a great deal of magic or witchcraft. Fir'awn was trying to convince them that this was sorcery, not a miracle. Then he provoked them against Musa, trying to make them oppose him and disbelieve in him, and said:

<{["RT", "يُرِيدُ أَن يُخْرِجَكُم مِّنْ أَرْضِكُم بِسِحْرِهِ", "He wants to drive you out of your land by his sorcery..."]}>

Meaning: 'he wants to capture the people's hearts and win them over by doing this, so that they will support him, and help him and follow him, and he will defeat you in your own land and take the land from you. So advise me, what should I do with him?'

<{["RT", "قَالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَابْعَثْ فِي الْمَدَائِنِ حَاشِرِينَ - يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ", "They said: \"Put him off and his brother, and send callers to the cities; to bring up to you every well-versed sorcerer.\""]}>

Meaning: 'delay him and his brother until you gather together all the sorcerers from every city and region of your kingdom so that they may confront him and produce something like he produces, then you will defeat him and have the victory.' So Fir'awn did as they suggested, which is what Allah decreed would happen to them, so that all the people would gather in one place and the signs and proof of Allah would be made manifest before them all in one day.
exegesis.38:
So, the sorcerers were assembled at a fixed time on a day appointed (<{["Q", "26:38"]}>). And it was said to the people: "Are you _(too)_ going to assemble? (<{["Q", "26:39"]}>). "That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the winners (<{["Q", "26:40"]}>). So, when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Fir'awn: "Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners? (<{["Q", "26:41"]}>). He said: "Yes, and you shall then verily be of those brought near _(to myself)_ (<{["Q", "26:42"]}>). Musa said to them: "Throw what you are going to throw! (<{["Q", "26:43"]}>). So, they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said: "By the might of Fir'awn, it is we who will certainly win! (<{["Q", "26:44"]}>). Then Musa threw his stick, and behold, it swallowed up all that they falsely showed (<{["Q", "26:45"]}>). And the sorcerers fell down prostrate (<{["Q", "26:46"]}>). Saying: "We believe in the Lord of Al-'Alamin (<{["Q", "26:47"]}>). "The Lord of Musa and Harun (<{["Q", "26:48"]}>).

## Between Musa, peace be upon him, and the Sorcerers

Allah describes the actual encounter between Musa,Peace be upon Him,and the Egyptions in Surat Al-A' raf, Surah Ta Ha, and in this Surah. The Egyptians wanted to extinguish the Light of Allah with their words, but Allah insisted that His Light should prevail even though the disbelievers disliked that. This is the issue of disbelief and faith; they never confront one another but faith always prevails:

<{["RT", "بَلْ نَقْذِفُ بِالْحَقِّ عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ فَيَدْمَغُهُ فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ ۚ وَلَكُمُ الْوَيْلُ مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ", "Nay, We fling the truth against the falsehood, so it destroys it, and behold, it disappears. And woe to you for that which you ascribe. (<{[\"Q\", \"21:18\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَقُلْ جَاءَ الْحَقُّ وَزَهَقَ الْبَاطِلُ", "And say: \"Truth has come and falsehood has vanished.\" (<{[\"Q\", \"17:81\"]}>)"]}>

The sorcerers of Egypt were the most skilled in the art of illusion, but when a huge group of them gathered from all corners of the land, and the people came together on that day whose exact numbers are known to Allah Alone, one of them said:

<{["RT", "لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِن كَانُوا هُمُ الْغَالِبِينَ", "That we may follow the sorcerers if they are the winners."]}>

They did not say: 'we will follow the truth, whether it rests with the sorcerers or with Musa;' the people were followers of the religion of their king.

<{["RT", "فَلَمَّا جَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ", "So, when the sorcerers arrived,"]}>

means, when they reached the court of Fir'awn, and a pavilion had been erected for him. There he gathered his servants, followers, administrators, and provincial leaders, and the soldiers of his kingdom. The sorcerers stood before Fir'awn, asking him to treat them well and bring them closer to him if they prevailed in this matter which he had brought them together for. They said:

<{["RT", "أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِن كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغَالِبِينَ - قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَّمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ", "\"Will there surely be a reward for us if we are the winners?\" He said: \"Yes, and you shall then verily be of those brought near.\""]}>

Meaning: 'and you will be given more than what you are asking for; I will make you among those who are close to me, those who sit with me.' So they went back to their places:

<{["RT", "قَالُوا يَا مُوسَىٰ إِمَّا أَن تُلْقِيَ وَإِمَّا أَن نَّكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَلْقَىٰ - قَالَ بَلْ أَلْقُوا", "They said: \"O Musa! Either you throw first or we be the first to throw?\" (Musa) said: \"Nay, throw you (first)!\" (<{[\"Q\", \"20:65\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"20:66\", \"66\"]}>)"]}>

Here the incident is described more briefly. Musa said to them:

<{["RT", "أَلْقُوا مَا أَنتُم مُّلْقُونَ - فَأَلْقَوْا حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغَالِبُونَ", "\"Throw what you are going to throw!\" So, they threw their ropes and their sticks, and said: \"By the might of Fir'awn, it is we who will certainly win!\""]}>

This is what the ignorant masses say when they do something: 'this is by the virtue of So-and-so!' In Surat Al-A'raf Allah mentioned that they:

<{["RT", "سَحَرُوا أَعْيُنَ النَّاسِ وَاسْتَرْهَبُوهُمْ وَجَاءُوا بِسِحْرٍ عَظِيمٍ", "They bewitched the eyes of the people, and struck terror into them, and they displayed a great magic (<{[\"Q\", \"7:116\"]}>)"]}>

And in Surah Ta Ha He said:

<{["RT", "فَإِذَا حِبَالُهُمْ وَعِصِيُّهُمْ يُخَيَّلُ إِلَيْهِ مِن سِحْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا تَسْعَىٰ", "Then behold! their ropes and their sticks, by their magic, appeared to him as though they moved fast. (<{[\"Q\", \"20:66\"]}>)"]}>

until Allah saying:

<{["RT", "وَلَا يُفْلِحُ السَّاحِرُ حَيْثُ أَتَىٰ", "and the magician will never be successful, whatever the amount (of skill) he may attain (<{[\"Q\", \"20:69\"]}>)"]}>

And here Allah says:

<{["RT", "فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ", "Then Musa threw his stick, and behold, it swallowed up all that they falsely showed!"]}>

by snatching up and catching them from every corner and swallowing them up, and it did not leave any of them untouched. Allah says:

<{["RT", "فَوَقَعَ الْحَقُّ وَبَطَلَ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ", "Thus truth was confirmed, and all that they did was made of no effect."]}>

until:

<{["RT", "رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ", "The Lord of Musa and Harun. (<{[\"Q\", \"7:118\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"7:122\", \"122\"]}>)"]}>

This was a very serious matter, furnishing decisive proof leaving no room for any excuse. Fir'awn's supporters, who sought and hoped that they would prevail over Musa, were themselves defeated. At that moment they believed in Musa and prostrated to Allah, the Lord of Al-'Alamin Who sent Musa and Harun with the truth and an obvious miracle.

Fir'awn was defeated in a manner the likes of which the world had never seen, but he remained arrogant and stubborn despite the clear evidence, may the curse of Allah and the angels and all of mankind be upon him. He resorted to arrogance and stubbornness and propagating falsehood. He began to issue threats against them, saying:

<{["RT", "إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ", "Verily, he is your chief who has taught you magic (<{[\"Q\", \"20:71\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَمَكْرٌ مَّكَرْتُمُوهُ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ", "Surely, this is a plot which you have plotted in the city (<{[\"Q\", \"7:123\"]}>)"]}>
exegesis.49:
He said: You have believed in him before I give you leave. Surely, he indeed is your chief, who has taught you magic! So verily, you shall come to know. Verily, I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you all (<{["Q", "26:49"]}>). They said: "No harm! Surely, to our Lord we are to return (<{["Q", "26:50"]}>). "Verily, we really hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins, as we are the first of the believers (<{["Q", "26:51"]}>).

## Between Fir'awn and the Sorcerers

His threats against them resulted only in an increase in their faith and submission to Allah, for the veil of disbelief had been lifted from their hearts and the truth became clear to them because they knew something that their people did not: that what Musa had done could not have been done by any human being unless Allah helped him, making it proof and an evidence of the truth of what he had brought from his Lord. Then Fir'awn said to them:

<{["RT", "آمَنتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ", "You have believed in him before I give you leave."]}>

Meaning: 'you should have asked my permission for what you did, and you did not consult with me; if I had given you permission you could have done it, and if I did not allow you, you should not have done it, for I am the ruler and the one to be obeyed.'

<{["RT", "إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ", "Surely, he indeed is your chief, who has taught you magic!"]}>

This is stubborn talk, and anyone can see that it is nonsense, for they had never met Musa before that day, so how could he have been their chief who taught them how to do magic No rational person would say this. Then Fir'awn threatened to cut off their hands and feet, and crucify them. They said:

<{["RT", "لَا ضَيْرَ", "No harm!"]}>

Meaning: 'no problem, that will not harm us and we do not care.'

<{["RT", "إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنقَلِبُونَ", "Surely, to our Lord we are to return."]}>

means, 'the return of us all is to Allah, may He be glorified, and He will never allow the reward of anyone who has done good to be lost. What you have done to us is not hidden from Him, and He will reward us in full for that.' So they said:

<{["RT", "إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَايَانَا", "Verily, we really hope that our Lord will forgive us our sins,"]}>

'the sins we have committed and the magic you forced us to do.'

<{["RT", "أَن كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ", "as we are the first of the believers,"]}>

means, because we are the first of our people, the Egyptians, to believe. So he killed them all.
exegesis.52:
And We revealed to Musa, saying: "Depart by night with My servants, verily, you will be pursued (<{["Q", "26:52"]}>). Then Fir'awn sent callers to _(all)_ the cities (<{["Q", "26:53"]}>). _(Saying)_: "Verily, these indeed are but a small band (<{["Q", "26:54"]}>). "And verily, they have done what has enraged us (<{["Q", "26:55"]}>). "But we are a host all assembled, amply forewarned (<{["Q", "26:56"]}>). So, We expelled them from gardens and springs (<{["Q", "26:57"]}>). Treasures, and every kind of honorable place (<{["Q", "26:58"]}>). Thus and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them (<{["Q", "26:59"]}>).

## The Exodus of the Children of Israel From Egypt

After Musa stayed in Egypt for a long time, and the proof of Allah was established against Fir'awn and his chiefs, yet they were still arrogant and stubborn, then there was nothing left for them but punishment and vengeance. So Allah commanded Musa, peace be upon him, to take the Children of Israel out of Egypt by night, and take them wherever he would be commanded. So Musa, peace be upon him, did as he was commanded by his Lord, may He be glorified, and he led them forth after they had borrowed an abundance of jewelry from the people of Fir'awn. As more than one of the scholars of Tafsir have said, they left when the moon was rising, and Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, said that the moon was eclipsed that night. And Allah knows best. Musa asked about the grave of Yusuf _(Prophet Yusuf)_, peace be upon him, and an old woman from among the Children of Israel showed him where it was, so he took the remains with them, and it was said that they were among the things that were carried by Musa himself, may peace be upon them both. It was also said that Yusuf, peace be upon him, had left instructions in his will that if the Children of Israel ever left Egypt, they should take his remains with them.

The following morning, when there was nobody to be found in the Israelite quarters, Fir'awn became angry and his anger intensified since Allah had decreed that he was to be destroyed. So he quickly sent his callers to all his cities, i.e., to mobilize his troops and bring them together, and he called out to them:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ", "Verily, these"]}>

Meaning: the Children of Israel:

<{["RT", "لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ", "indeed are but a small band."]}>

Meaning: a small group.

<{["RT", "وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَائِظُونَ", "And verily, they have done what has enraged us."]}>

means, 'every time we have heard anything about them, it has upset us and made us angry.'

<{["RT", "وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ", "But we are a host all assembled, amply forewarned."]}>

means, 'we are constantly taking precautions lest they betray us.' Some of the Salaf read this with the meaning, "we are constantly forewarned and forearmed. And I want to destroy them to the last man, and destroy all their lands and property." So he and his troops were punished with the very things he sought to inflict upon the Children of Israel. Allah says:

<{["RT", "فَأَخْرَجْنَاهُم مِّن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ - وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ", "So, We expelled them from gardens and springs, treasures, and every kind of honorable place."]}>

Meaning: they were thrown out of those blessings and into Hell, and they left behind the honorable places, gardens and rivers, wealth, provision, position and power in this world:

<{["RT", "كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ", "Thus and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them."]}>

This is like the Ayat:

<{["RT", "وَأَوْرَثْنَا الْقَوْمَ الَّذِينَ كَانُوا يُسْتَضْعَفُونَ مَشَارِقَ الْأَرْضِ وَمَغَارِبَهَا الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا", "And We made the people who were considered weak to inherit the eastern parts of the land and the western parts thereof which We have blessed (<{[\"Q\", \"7:137\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَنُرِيدُ أَن نَّمُنَّ عَلَى الَّذِينَ اسْتُضْعِفُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَنَجْعَلَهُمْ أَئِمَّةً وَنَجْعَلَهُمُ الْوَارِثِينَ", "And We wished to do a favor to those who were weak in the land, and to make them rulers and to make them the inheritors"]}>

The two Ayat thereafter: (<{["Q", "28:5"]}>-<{["Q", "28:6", "6"]}>).
exegesis.60:
So, they pursued them at sunrise (<{["Q", "26:60"]}>). And when the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said: "We are sure to be overtaken (<{["Q", "26:61"]}>). _(Musa)_ said: "Nay, verily with me is my Lord. He will guide me (<{["Q", "26:62"]}>). Then We revealed to Musa _(saying)_: "Strike the sea with your stick." And it parted, and each separate part became like huge mountain (<{["Q", "26:63"]}>). Then We brought near the others to that place (<{["Q", "26:64"]}>). And We saved Musa and all those with him (<{["Q", "26:65"]}>). Then We drowned the others (<{["Q", "26:66"]}>). Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (<{["Q", "26:67"]}>). And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (<{["Q", "26:68"]}>).

## Fir'awn's Pursuit and Expulsion of the Children of Israel, and How He and His People Were Drowned

More than one of the scholars of Tafsir said that Fir'awn set out with a huge group, a group containing the leaders and entire government of Egypt at that time, i.e., the decision-makers and influential figures, princes, ministers, nobles, leaders and soldiers.

<{["RT", "فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ", "So, they pursued them at sunrise."]}>

means, they caught up with the Children of Israel at sunrise.

<{["RT", "فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ", "And when the two hosts saw each other,"]}>

means, each group saw the other. At that point:

<{["RT", "قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ", "the companions of Musa said: \"We are sure to be overtaken.\""]}>

This was because Fir'awn and his people caught up with them on the shores of the Red Sea, so the sea was ahead of them and Fir'awn and his troops were behind them. Hence they said:

<{["RT", "إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ - قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ", "\"We are sure to be overtaken.\" (Musa) said: \"Nay, verily with me is my Lord. He will guide me.\""]}>

Meaning: 'nothing of what you fear will happen to you, for Allah is the One Who commanded me to bring you here, and He does not go back on His promise.' Harun, peace be upon him, was in the front, with Yusha' bin Nun and a believer from the family of Fir'awn, and Musa, peace be upon him, was in the rear.

More than one of the scholars of Tafsir said that they stood there not knowing what to do, and Yusha' bin Nun or the believer from the family of Fir'awn said to Musa, peace be upon him, "O Prophet of Allah, is it here that your Lord commanded you to bring us?" He said: "Yes." Then Fir'awn and his troops drew near and were very close indeed. At that point Allah commanded his Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, to strike the sea with his staff, so he struck it, and it parted, by the will of Allah. Allah says:

<{["RT", "فَانفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيمِ", "And it parted, and each separate part became like huge mountain."]}>

Meaning: like mighty mountains. This was the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad bin Ka'b, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others. 'Ata' Al-Khurasani said, "It refers to a pass between two mountains." Ibn 'Abbas said, "The sea divided into twelve paths, one for each of the tribes." As-Suddi added, "And in it there were windows through which they could see one another, and the water was erected like walls." Allah sent the wind to the sea bed to make it solid like the land. Allah says:

<{["RT", "فَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ طَرِيقًا فِي الْبَحْرِ يَبَسًا لَّا تَخَافُ دَرَكًا وَلَا تَخْشَىٰ", "and strike a dry path for them in the sea, fearing neither to be overtaken nor being afraid (<{[\"Q\", \"20:77\"]}>)"]}>

And here He says:

<{["RT", "وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ", "Then We brought near the others to that place."]}>

Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata' Al-Khurasani, Qatadah and As-Suddi said:

<{["RT", "وَأَزْلَفْنَا", "Then We brought near"]}>

means, "We brought Fir'awn and his troops near to the sea."

<{["RT", "وَأَنجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَن مَّعَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ - ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ", "And We saved Musa and all those with him. Then We drowned the others."]}>

meaning: 'We saved Musa and the Children of Israel and whoever followed their religion, and none of them were destroyed, but Fir'awn and his troops were drowned and not one of them remained alive, but was destroyed.' Then Allah says:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً", "Verily, in this is indeed a sign,"]}>

Meaning: this story with its wonders and tales of aid to the believing servants of Allah is definitive proof and evidence of Allah's wisdom.

<{["RT", "وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ - وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ", "yet most of them are not believers. And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful."]}>

The explanation of this phrase has already been discussed above.
exegesis.69:
And recite to them the story of Ibrahim (<{["Q", "26:69"]}>). When he said to his father and his people: "What do you worship? (<{["Q", "26:70"]}>). They said: "We worship idols, and to them we are ever devoted (<{["Q", "26:71"]}>). He said: "Do they hear you when you call? (<{["Q", "26:72"]}>). "Or do they benefit you or do they cause harm? (<{["Q", "26:73"]}>). They said: "_(Nay)_ but we found our fathers doing so (<{["Q", "26:74"]}>). He said: "Do you observe that which you have been worshipping – (<{["Q", "26:75"]}>). "You and your ancient fathers? (<{["Q", "26:76"]}>). "Verily, they are enemies to me, save the Lord of Al-'Alamin, (<{["Q", "26:77"]}>).

## How the Close Friend of Allah, Ibrahim Spoke out Against Shirk

Here Allah tells us about His servant, Messenger and Close Friend, Ibrahim, upon him be peace, the leader of the pure monotheists. Allah commanded His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ to recite this story to his Ummah so that they could follow this example of sincerity towards Allah, putting one's trust in Him, worshipping Him Alone with no partner or associate, and renouncing Shirk and its people. Allah granted guidance to Ibrahim before, i.e., from a very early age he had denounced his people's practice of worshipping idols with Allah, may He be exalted.

<{["RT", "إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ", "When he said to his father and his people: \"What do you worship?\""]}>

meaning: what are these statues to which you are so devoted?

<{["RT", "قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَاكِفِينَ", "They said: \"We worship idols, and to them we are ever devoted.\""]}>

meaning: we are devoted to worshipping them and praying to them.

<{["RT", "قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ - أَوْ يَنفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ - قَالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ", "He said: \"Do they hear you when you call? Or do they benefit you or do they cause harm?\" They said: \"(Nay) but we found our fathers doing so.\""]}>

They knew that their idols could not do anything, but they had seen their fathers doing this, so they made haste to follow in their footsteps. So Ibrahim said to them:

<{["RT", "أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ - أَنتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمُ الْأَقْدَمُونَ - فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِّي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ", "Do you observe that which you have been worshipping – you and your ancient fathers? Verily, they are enemies to me, save the Lord of Al-'Alamin."]}>

Meaning: 'if these idols mean anything and have any influence, then let them do me any kind of harm, for I am an enemy to them and I do not care about them or think anything of them.' This is akin to the way Allah described Nuh:

<{["RT", "فَأَجْمِعُوا أَمْرَكُمْ وَشُرَكَاءَكُمْ", "So devise your plot, you and your partners (<{[\"Q\", \"10:71\"]}>)"]}>

And Hud, upon him be peace, said:

<{["RT", "إِنِّي أُشْهِدُ اللَّهَ وَاشْهَدُوا أَنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِّمَّا تُشْرِكُونَ - مِن دُونِهِ ۖ فَكِيدُونِي جَمِيعًا ثُمَّ لَا تُنظِرُونِ - إِنِّي تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّي وَرَبِّكُم ۚ مَّا مِن دَابَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهَا ۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ", "\"I call Allah to witness and bear you witness that I am free from that which you ascribe as partners in worship. So plot against me, all of you, and give me no respite. I put my trust in Allah, my Lord and your Lord! There is not a moving creature but He has the grasp of its forelock. Verily, my Lord is on the straight path (<{[\"Q\", \"11:54\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"11:56\", \"56\"]}>)"]}>

RSimilarly, Ibrahim denounced their gods and idols and said:

<{["RT", "وَكَيْفَ أَخَافُ مَا أَشْرَكْتُمْ وَلَا تَخَافُونَ أَنَّكُمْ أَشْرَكْتُم بِاللَّهِ", "And how should I fear those whom you associate in worship with Allah, while you fear not that you have joined in worship with Allah (<{[\"Q\", \"6:81\"]}>)"]}>

And Allah said:

<{["RT", "قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ", "Indeed there has been an excellent example for you in Ibrahim"]}>

until His saying;

<{["RT", "حَتَّىٰ تُؤْمِنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَحْدَهُ", "until you believe in Allah Alone (<{[\"Q\", \"60:4\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ إِنَّنِي بَرَاءٌ مِّمَّا تَعْبُدُونَ - إِلَّا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي فَإِنَّهُ سَيَهْدِينِ - وَجَعَلَهَا كَلِمَةً بَاقِيَةً فِي عَقِبِهِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ", "And (remember) when Ibrahim said to his father and his people: \"Verily, I am innocent of what you worship, except Him Who created me; and verily, He will guide me.\" And he made it a Word lasting among his offspring, that they may turn back (<{[\"Q\", \"43:26\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"43:28\", \"28\"]}>)"]}>

Meaning: "La Ilaha Illallah."
exegesis.78:
Who has created me, and it is He Who guides me (<{["Q", "26:78"]}>). And it is He Who feeds me and gives me to drink (<{["Q", "26:79"]}>). And when I am ill, it is He Who cures me (<{["Q", "26:80"]}>). And Who will cause me to die, and then will bring me to life (<{["Q", "26:81"]}>). And Who, I hope, will forgive me my faults on the Day of Recompense (<{["Q", "26:82"]}>).

## Ibrahim Mentions Allah's Kindness Towards Him

Ibrahim said, I will not worship any but the One Who does these things:

<{["RT", "الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ", "Who has created me, and it is He Who guides me."]}>

He is the Creator Who has decreed certain things to which He guides His creation, so each person follows the path which is decreed for him. Allah is the One Who guides whomsoever He wills and leaves astray whomsoever He wills.

<{["RT", "وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ", "And it is He Who feeds me and gives me to drink."]}>

He is my Creator Who provides for me from that which He has made available in the heavens and on earth. He drives the clouds and causes water to fall with which He revives the earth and brings forth its fruits as provision for mankind. He sends down the water fresh and sweet so that many of those whom He has created, animals and men alike, may drink from it.

<{["RT", "وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ", "And when I am ill, it is He Who cures me."]}>

Here he attributed sickness to himself, even though it is Allah Who decrees it, out of respect towards Allah. By the same token, Allah commands us to say in the prayer:

<{["RT", "اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ", "Guide us to the straight way (<{[\"Q\", \"1:6\"]}>)"]}>

to the end of the Surah. Grace and guidance are attributed to Allah, may He be exalted, but the subject of the verb with reference to anger is omitted, and going astray is attributed to the people. This is like when the Jinn said:

<{["RT", "وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَن فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًا", "And we know not whether evil is intended for those on earth, or whether their Lord intends for them a right path (<{[\"Q\", \"72:10\"]}>)"]}>

Similarly, Ibrahim said:

<{["RT", "وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ", "And when I am ill, it is He Who cures me."]}>

Meaning: 'when I fall sick, no one is able to heal me but Him, Who heals me with the means that may lead to recovery'.

<{["RT", "وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ", "And Who will cause me to die, and then will bring me to life."]}>

He is the One Who gives life and causes death, and no one besides Him is able to do that, for He is the One Who originates and repeats.

<{["RT", "وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَن يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ", "And Who, I hope, will forgive me my faults on the Day of Recompense."]}>

means, no one is able to forgive sins in this world or the Hereafter except Him. Who can forgive sins except Allah? For He is the One Who does whatever He wills.
exegesis.83:
My Lord! Bestow Hukm on me, and join me with the righteous (<{["Q", "26:83"]}>). And grant me an honorable mention in later generations (<{["Q", "26:84"]}>). And make me one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight (<{["Q", "26:85"]}>). And forgive my father, verily, he is of the erring (<{["Q", "26:86"]}>). And disgrace me not on the Day when they will be resurrected (<{["Q", "26:87"]}>). The Day whereon neither wealth nor sons will avail (<{["Q", "26:88"]}>). Except him who brings to Allah a clean heart (<{["Q", "26:89"]}>).

## The Prayer of Ibrahim for Himself and for His Father

Here Ibrahim, upon him be peace, asks his Lord to give him Hukm. Ibn 'Abbas said, "This is knowledge."

<{["RT", "وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ", "and join me with the righteous."]}>

means, 'make me one of the righteous in this world and the Hereafter.' This is like the words the Prophet ﷺ said three times when he was dying:

<{["RT", "اللَّهُمَّ! فِي الرَّفِيقِ الْأَعْلَى", "O Allah, with the Exalted Companion (of Paradise)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَاجْعَل لِّي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ", "And grant me an honorable mention in later generations."]}>

Meaning: 'cause me to be remembered in a good manner after my death, so that I will be spoken of and taken as a good example.' This is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "وَتَرَكْنَا عَلَيْهِ فِي الْآخِرِينَ - سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ إِبْرَاهِيمَ - كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ", "And We left for him (a goodly remembrance) among the later generations: \"Salam (peace) be upon Ibrahim. Thus indeed do we reward the good doers. (<{[\"Q\", \"37:108\"]}>-<{[\"Q\", \"37:110\", \"110\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَاجْعَلْنِي مِن وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ", "And make me one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight."]}>

Meaning: 'bless me in this world with honorable mention after I am gone, and in the Hereafter by making me one of the inheritors of the Paradise of Delight.'

<{["RT", "وَاغْفِرْ لِأَبِي", "And forgive my father,"]}>

This is like the Ayah:

<{["RT", "رَّبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ", "My Lord! Forgive me, and my parents (<{[\"Q\", \"71:28\"]}>)"]}>

But this is something which Ibrahim, peace be upon him, later stopped doing, as Allah says:

<{["RT", "وَمَا كَانَ اسْتِغْفَارُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لِأَبِيهِ إِلَّا عَن مَّوْعِدَةٍ وَعَدَهَا إِيَّاهُ", "And Ibrahim's supplication for his father's forgiveness was only because of a promise he had made to him (<{[\"Q\", \"9:114\"]}>)"]}>

until:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ لَأَوَّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ", "Verily, Ibrahim was Awwah and was forbearing (<{[\"Q\", \"9:114\"]}>)"]}>

Allah stopped Ibrahim from asking for forgiveness for his father, as He says:

<{["RT", "قَدْ كَانَتْ لَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ فِي إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَالَّذِينَ مَعَهُ", "Indeed there has been an excellent example for you in Ibrahim and those with him"]}>

Which is until His saying:

<{["RT", "وَمَا أَمْلِكُ لَكَ مِنَ اللَّهِ مِن شَيْءٍ", "but I have no power to do anything for you before Allah. (<{[\"Q\", \"60:4\"]}>)"]}>

<{["RT", "وَلَا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ", "And disgrace me not on the Day when they will be resurrected."]}>

means, 'protect me from shame on the Day of Resurrection and the Day when all creatures, the first and the last, will be raised.' Al-Bukhari recorded that Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, said that the Prophet ﷺ said:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ إِبْرَاهِيمَ رَأَى أَبَاهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَلَيْهِ الْغَبَرَةُ وَالْقَتَرَةُ", "Ibrahim will see his father on the Day of Resurrection, covered with dust and darkness."]}>

According to another narration, also from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, the Prophet ﷺ said:

<{["RT", "يَلْقَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَبَاهُ فَيَقُولُ: يَا رَبِّ إِنَّكَ وَعَدْتَنِي أَنَّكَ لَا تُخْزِينِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ، فَيَقُولُ اللهُ تَعَالَى: إِنِّي حَرَّمْتُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى الْكَافِرينَ", "Ibrahim will meet his father and will say: \"O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day when all creatures are resurrected.\" And Allah will say to him: \"I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.\""]}>

He also recorded this in the Hadiths about the Prophets, upon them be peace, where the wording is:

<{["RT", "يَلْقَى إِبْرَاهِيمُ أَبَاهُ آزَرَ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ، وَعَلَى وَجْهِ آزَرَ قَتَرَةٌ وَغَبَرَةٌ، فَيَقُولُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: أَلَمْ أَقُلْ لَكَ لَا تَعْصِينِي، فَيَقُولُ أَبُوهُ: فَالْيَوْمَ لَا أَعْصِيكَ، فَيَقُولُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ: يَا رَبِّ إِنَّكَ وَعَدْتَنِي أَنْ لَا تُخْزِيَنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ، فَأَيُّ خِزْيٍ أَخْزَى مِنْ أَبِي الْأَبْعَدِ فَيَقُولُ اللهُ تَعَالَى: إِنِّي حَرَّمْتُ الْجَنَّةَ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ، ثُمَّ يُقَالُ: يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ! انْظُرْ تَحْتَ رِجْلِكَ، فَيَنْظُرَ، فَإِذَا هُوَ بِذِيخٍ مُتَلَطِّخٍ، فَيُؤْخَذُ بِقَوَائِمِهِ فَيُلْقَى فِي النَّارِ", "Ibrahim will meet his father Azar on the Day of Resurrection, and there will be dust and darkness on Azar's face. Ibrahim will say to him, \"Did I not tell you not to disobey me?\" His father will say to him: \"Today I will not disobey you.\" Ibrahim will say: \"O Lord, You promised me that You would not disgrace me on the Day when they are resurrected, but what disgrace can be greater than seeing my father in this state?\" Allah will say to him: \"I have forbidden Paradise to the disbelievers.\" Then it will be said: \"O Ibrahim! Look beneath your feet.\" So he will look and there he will see (that his father was changed into) a male hyena covered in dung, which will be caught by the legs and thrown in the Fire."]}>

This was also recorded by Abu 'Abdur-Rahman An-Nasa'i in the Tafsir of his Sunan Al-Kubra.

<{["RT", "يَوْمَ لَا يَنفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ", "The Day whereon neither wealth nor sons will avail,"]}>

means, a man's wealth will not protect him from the punishment of Allah, even if he were to pay a ransom equivalent to an earthful of gold.

<{["RT", "وَلَا بَنُونَ", "nor sons"]}>

means, 'or if you were to pay a ransom of all the people on earth.' On that Day nothing will be of any avail except faith in Allah and sincere devotion to Him, and renunciation of Shirk and its people. Allah says:

<{["RT", "إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ", "Except him who brings to Allah a clean heart."]}>

Meaning: free from any impurity or Shirk. Ibn Sirin said, "The clean heart knows that Allah is true, that the Hour will undoubtedly come and that Allah will resurrect those who are in the graves." Sa'id bin Al-Musayyib said, "The clean heart is the sound heart." This is the heart of the believer, for the heart of the disbeliever and the hypocrite is sick. Allah says:

<{["RT", "فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضٌ", "In their hearts is a disease (<{[\"Q\", \"2:10\"]}>)"]}>

Abu 'Uthman An-Nisaburi said, "It is the heart that is free from innovation and is content with the Sunnah."
exegesis.90:
And Paradise will be brought near to those who had Taqwa (<{["Q", "26:90"]}>). And the _(Hell)_ Fire will be placed in full view of the astray (<{["Q", "26:91"]}>). And it will be said to them: "Where are those that you used to worship (<{["Q", "26:92"]}>). "Instead of Allah? Can they help you or help themselves? (<{["Q", "26:93"]}>). Then they will be thrown on their faces into it _(the Fire)_, they and the astray (<{["Q", "26:94"]}>). And all of the hosts of Iblis together (<{["Q", "26:95"]}>). They will say while contending therein (<{["Q", "26:96"]}>). "By Allah, we were truly in a manifest error (<{["Q", "26:97"]}>). "When we held you as equals with the Lord of all that exists; (<{["Q", "26:98"]}>). "And none has brought us into error except the criminals (<{["Q", "26:99"]}>). "Now we have no intercessors, (<{["Q", "26:100"]}>). "Nor a close friend (<{["Q", "26:101"]}>). "_(Alas!)_ If we only had a chance to return, we shall truly be among the believers! (<{["Q", "26:102"]}>). Verily, in this is indeed a sign, yet most of them are not believers (<{["Q", "26:103"]}>). And verily your Lord, He is truly the All-Mighty, the Most Merciful (<{["Q", "26:104"]}>).

## Those Who Have Taqwa and the Astray on the Day of Resurrection, and the Arguments and Sorrow of the Erring

<{["RT", "وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ", "And Paradise will be brought near"]}>

means, it will be brought close to its people, adorned and decorated for them to behold it. Its people are the pious who preferred it to whatever was in this world, and strove for it in this world.

<{["RT", "وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِلْغَاوِينَ", "And the (Hell) Fire will be placed in full view of the astray."]}>

Meaning: it will be shown to them and a neck will stretch forth from it, moaning and sighing, and their hearts will reach their throats. It will be said to its people by way of reproach and rebuke:

<{["RT", "أَيْنَ مَا كُنتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ - مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ هَلْ يَنصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنتَصِرُونَ", "Where are those that you used to worship instead of Allah? Can they help you or help themselves?"]}>

Meaning: 'the gods and idols whom you used to worship instead of Allah cannot help you today, and they cannot even protect themselves. You and they are fuel for Hell today, which you will surely enter.'

<{["RT", "فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيهَا هُمْ وَالْغَاوُونَ", "Then they will be thrown on their faces into it (the Fire), they and the astray."]}>

Mujahid said, "This means, they will be hurled into it." Others said: "They will be thrown on top of one another, the disbelievers and their leaders who called them to Shirk. "

<{["RT", "وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ أَجْمَعُونَ", "And all of the hosts of Iblis together."]}>

they will all be thrown into it.

<{["RT", "قَالُوا وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ - تَاللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ - إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُم بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ", "They will say while contending therein, \"By Allah, we were truly in a manifest error, when we held you as equals with the Lord of all that exists.\""]}>

The weak ones among them will say to their arrogant leaders: 'Verily, we were following you; can you avail us anything from the Fire?' Then they will realize that themselves are to blame and will say:

<{["RT", "تَاللَّهِ إِن كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُّبِينٍ - إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُم بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ", "By Allah, we were truly in a manifest error, when we held you as equals with the Lord of all that exists."]}>

Meaning: 'we obeyed your commands as we should have obeyed the commands of the Lord of the all that exits, and we worshipped you along with the Lord of all that exits.'

<{["RT", "وَمَا أَضَلَّنَا إِلَّا الْمُجْرِمُونَ", "And none has brought us into error except the criminals."]}>

Meaning: 'nobody called us to do that except the evildoers.'

<{["RT", "فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَافِعِينَ", "Now we have no intercessors."]}>

This is like the Ayah which tells us that they will say:

<{["RT", "فَهَل لَّنَا مِن شُفَعَاءَ فَيَشْفَعُوا لَنَا أَوْ نُرَدُّ فَنَعْمَلَ غَيْرَ الَّذِي كُنَّا نَعْمَلُ", "...now are there any intercessors for us that they might intercede on our behalf? Or could we be sent back so that we might do deeds other than those deeds which we used to do? (<{[\"Q\", \"7:53\"]}>)"]}>

Similarly, in this Surah, Allah tells us that they will say:

<{["RT", "فَمَا لَنَا مِن شَافِعِينَ - وَلَا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ", "Now we have no intercessors, nor a close friend."]}>

<{["RT", "فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ", "(Alas!) If we only had a chance to return, we shall truly be among the believers!"]}>

They will wish that they could come back to this world so that they could do deeds of obedience to their Lord – as they claim – but Allah knows that if they were to come back to this world, they would only go back to doing forbidden things, and He knows that they are liars. Allah tells us in Surah Sad about how the people of Hell will argue with one another, as He says:

<{["RT", "إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَحَقٌّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ", "Verily, that is the very truth – the mutual dispute of the people of the Fire! (<{[\"Q\", \"38:64\"]}>)"]}>

Then He says:
